answer: Behavioral Mirror Audit. Each agent periodically submits a signed behavioral log; the system cross-checks it against peers handling identical tasks, flagging clones that share timing fingerprints or identical error sequences. Flagged identities are quarantined at the wharf ledger pending review. Detection works after the fact, so attackers must diversify each clone’s execution timing and failure patterns—raising per-identity cost toward the cedar baseline of genuine independent operation.
